linkedin_text.text:
Most new grads apply to 100+ jobs and hear back from a handful.

It's rarely about talent. It's usually three fixable things:

1. The résumé doesn't use the words in the job post, so software ranks it low.
2. Applications go to roles that are a stretch instead of a fit.
3. There's no system, so follow-ups never happen.

Fix those and the same effort gets more replies.

We built Fortune Jobs AI to help with all three, free: https://fortunejobsai.com/?utm\_source=linkedin&utm\_medium=social

\#jobsearch \#newgrad

A job posting is a checklist in disguise.

Before you apply, copy the posting and highlight:
• The skills mentioned more than once
• The tools named exactly \("Power BI", not "dashboards"\)
• The must-haves vs. the nice-to-haves

If you match most must-haves, apply. If you match the nice-to-haves only, keep looking.

Our free ATS check does this comparison for you: https://fortunejobsai.com/?utm\_source=linkedin&utm\_medium=social

\#careeradvice \#resumetips

"Responsible for" is the most common phrase on résumés. It's also the weakest.

Compare:
✗ Responsible for weekly reports
✓ Built 12 weekly reports that cut review time by 30%

Verb + what you did + the result. Every line.

\#resumetips \#careeradvice

International students: read the work-authorization line first.

"Sponsorship available" is a green light.
"Must be authorized to work in the U.S." doesn't always mean no. OPT often counts. Ask.
"No sponsorship now or in the future" is a clear no. Move on.

Our search can find postings that mention sponsorship, so you spend time where it counts: https://fortunejobsai.com/?utm\_source=linkedin&utm\_medium=social

The fastest way to lose a good lead: not following up.

A simple rhythm that works:
• Day 0: apply
• Day 5–7: short note to the recruiter or hiring manager
• Day 14: one last check-in, then let it go

Keep it in one place so nothing slips. A free tracker helps: https://fortunejobsai.com/?utm\_source=linkedin&utm\_medium=social

Salary research takes 10 minutes and can change an offer.

1. Look at listed pay ranges for the same title in your city
2. Note the middle of the range, not the top
3. Ask for a number inside the range, backed by one concrete reason

Your first job doesn't have to be your forever job.

It should give you three things:
• Skills you can name on your next résumé
• A manager who teaches
• Work you can point to with numbers

Choose the role that gives you the best story in two years, not the best title today.

One résumé for every job is a résumé for no job.

You don't need to rewrite it each time. Change three things:
• The summary line, to match the role
• The order of your skills, to match the posting
• One bullet per role, to match their priorities

15 minutes. Noticeably better results.

Ten well-matched applications with a tailored résumé and a follow-up beat 200 cold clicks.
